# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

Calculate the Guilty majority on every trial and identify how many votes are needed to change the result. A tied or near-majority Guilty vote still acquits, and an acquittal can cost the village another night.

Weigh exact-role evidence against a role claim more heavily than a superficial role-name conflict. Repeated roles are allowed, so a dead player having a role does not by itself disprove another claim; a credible exact-role result can.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's result established that Carol and Erin visited Dave, but not which one attacked him. Keeping that distinction clear avoided treating either visit alone as proof; later evidence was needed to identify Erin.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once.
tips_feedback.why: The rule is correct, but emphasizing the possibility of a second Sheriff contributed to acquitting Erin on Day 2. Erin was the Yakuza Pharmacist, and that delay let the Yakuza kill Heidi the next night. The possibility of duplicate roles should prevent a claim from being ruled out solely on that basis, not outweigh other risk signals.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang.
tips_feedback.why: On Erin's later trial, Alice's claimed Profiler result gave a specific exact-role conflict with Erin's Sheriff claim. Erin's Pharmacist flip confirmed the claim was false; this was stronger evidence than the earlier duplicate-Sheriff argument.

summary: The Village won 5-of-9 survivors to zero Yakuza. Dave hinted at Sheriff on Day 1 ("I'll report any Sheriff check I get"), and Heidi's public follow-up drew more attention to it, so the Yakuza killed him on Night 1. Erin held the Katana and was a Pharmacist. She visited Dave with it, and Heidi's Lookout watch caught her. Erin then fake-claimed Sheriff, the role Dave had just flipped. That was close to a confession. She still survived Day 2 on a 4-4 vote, because two Good players, Heidi and Ivan, accepted 'roles can repeat' and Bob voted Innocent beside them. On Day 2 Grace said publicly that she had protected Heidi. The Yakuza blocked Grace on Night 2 and killed Heidi. On Day 3 Alice's Profiler result on Erin (Cartographer/Pharmacist/Smuggler) settled the case, and Erin was hanged; Bob's late Guilty bus came too late to help him. Bob saved his Smuggler swaps until Night 3. There he swapped Alice and Carol so that the Katana and Grace's protection both landed on the wrong player, and Alice died. By then, though, Carol's Night 1 census (one Evil among Bob, Dave and Heidi) plus Dave's and Heidi's Good flips pointed squarely at Bob. His No and Innocent votes for Erin also linked him to her. He was hanged on Day 4.

lessons.tip: When a Lookout's result names two visitors to a Katana victim and one of them has a confirmed, harmless explanation, treat the other as near-proven. A claim of a role that has just flipped dead is not saved by 'roles can repeat'. Hang on the first chance instead of waiting for more confirmation.
lessons.evidence: Day 2: Heidi saw only Carol and Erin visit Dave. Carol's census visit was confirmed, and Erin claimed the dead Dave's Sheriff role. Heidi and Ivan voted Innocent on the 'duplicates allowed' caveat, Erin survived 4-4, and she got another night to kill Heidi.

lessons.tip: Never fake-claim a role that has just been revealed on a flip, and plan a cover story for any visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen before the Day starts. If the holder's visit gets exposed, move the Katana to a teammate.
lessons.evidence: Erin claimed Sheriff the morning after Dave flipped Sheriff, and she kept the Katana after Heidi named her. A Profiler result later finished her off, and her Sheriff claim had been the town's main case from Day 2 onward.

lessons.tip: Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. If someone else does, don't ask them about it in public, because that only spreads the hint further.
lessons.evidence: Dave said he would 'report any Sheriff check I get.' Heidi asked if that was a role claim, and the Yakuza killed Dave on Night 1, citing exactly that wording.

lessons.tip: Don't reveal whom you protected while that player is still a likely target. The Pharmacist will simply block you on the night it matters.
lessons.evidence: Grace said on Day 2 that she had protected Heidi. In night chat Bob proposed blocking Grace for that reason, and Erin did so on Night 2. Heidi then died to the Katana.

lessons.tip: Combine census counts with confirmed flips to pin down one player. Repeat the logic every day as new deaths remove the other options.
lessons.evidence: Carol's Night 1 census found one Evil among Bob, Dave and Heidi. Once Dave and Heidi both flipped Good, that left Bob, and he was hanged on Day 4.

lessons.tip: Profile anyone with a contested claim. Also read your earlier profiles for which non-Good roles they show to be in play.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Night 1 profile of Ivan already listed Pharmacist and Smuggler as roles in play. Her Night 2 profile of Erin gave the same three roles and ruled out Sheriff, which got Erin hanged on Day 3.

lessons.tip: Use your swaps while a teammate is under pressure, for example to send a Lookout or Tracker onto the wrong player or to redirect protection. Also don't volunteer denials about mechanics nobody asked about, because that hints at your role.
lessons.evidence: Bob held both tokens through Nights 1-2 while Erin was exposed. His one swap on Night 3 sent Grace's protection to the wrong player and killed Alice. On Day 2 he said unprompted that he 'wasn't told I was swapped', and Carol and Frank pressed him on it more than once.

lessons.tip: After a Yakuza flips, look first at whoever voted No and Innocent for them. Pairs who protect each other in every vote are likely partners.
lessons.evidence: Bob voted No on Erin's nominations and Innocent at her Day 2 trial, and Erin did the same for him. After Erin flipped Pharmacist, the town cited that pattern alongside the census and hanged Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action... A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Frank, Grace and Alice used this logic against Erin. The players who instead leaned on 'a visit isn't an attack' (Heidi, Ivan) acquitted Erin on Day 2.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat
tips_feedback.why: Heidi, Ivan, Bob and Erin all invoked 'roles can repeat' to acquit Erin's obviously false Sheriff claim on Day 2. That cost Heidi her life.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Erin turned it into the stalling line 'what fact has been disproved?'. Good voters held out for proof against a near-certain Lookout result.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at your power role on Day 1.
tips_feedback.why: Dave ignored it with his 'Sheriff check' wording and was the first Katana kill.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM
tips_feedback.why: Grace revealed that she had protected Heidi, a past target but an obvious repeat. The Yakuza blocked her, and Heidi died on Night 2, which shows the cost of the leak.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict
tips_feedback.why: Erin broke it by claiming the just-revealed Sheriff role after a Lookout had seen her visit. The claim was the core of the town's case against her.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored it and kept the Katana on Erin after Heidi named her. She was the exposed, central suspect until her hanging.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's No and Innocent votes for Erin were cited alongside Carol's census, and Bob was hanged right after Erin's flip.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents can save them, defend them.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 2 Bob's Innocent vote helped save Erin 4-4. On Day 3 he bused her when she was doomed. Even so, the Day 2 defense later counted against him.

issues.description: Night 3: Grace chose to protect Alice (the night-action log says 'target Alice'). Bob's swap redirected the protection to Carol. Grace's night history then showed her submitted target as Carol, while her result said Alice, as R23 requires. The history field showed the landed target, not the chosen one. This leaked the swap that R23 says results must not reveal. Grace raised it publicly on Day 4 and in feedback, and it confused several players.

The profile op threw a ValueError ('a Profiler can't target themselves') when a Smuggler swap redirected Alice's profile of Carol onto Alice herself. The program has no path for a swap-redirected action landing on its own user, so the moderator had to resolve the result and the token count by hand.

R23 says a swapped action lands 'as if its user had chosen that player'. The rules don't say what happens when that player is the user and the role forbids self-targeting (Profiler: 'other than yourself'). The moderator treated it as a valid self-profile with a self-visit. Fizzling the action, or the visit not counting, would also be defensible readings. The same gap applies to Medic, Surveyor, Census Taker and others.

Several players misread R3 on Day 4. Frank said 'Standard protection on Alice can't stop a Standard Katana kill', but an attack must be strictly higher than the Defense, so it would stop it. Bob's post-game feedback called Alice's death a rules contradiction, although he had swapped Alice and Carol himself, so the protection landed on Carol. Alice's feedback likewise saw a mismatch. None accounted for R23's rule that results name the chosen target.

Players repeatedly misread the Scout result. On Day 2 Frank said his Scout result confirmed Ivan's 8/1 sizes and claimed 'Frank's group (8)', but Scout reports only one name per group and the group count, not sizes. Bob and Ivan had to correct this.

Alice misstated her own results on Day 3: 'My N1 and N2 profiles of Erin', when N1 was actually Ivan. Grace and Alice also kept saying Erin had given no check wording after Erin had stated 'Not Evil'.

Alice's N1 profile of Ivan and N2 profile of Erin returned exactly the same three-role set (Cartographer, Pharmacist, Smuggler). This is legal under random drawing, but it's a notable coincidence worth checking for draw or caching bugs. Players flagged it as suspicious.
Frank's Day 4 turn produced an empty answer (finish_reason length) and needed a retry.
Alice reported that the notepad, reason and feedback fields were required even when answering a survey question, which made the interface awkward.
